title_en: Zhang Chengyin v. Xuzhou Municipal People's Government — dispute over administrative reconsideration decision on house registration
ruling_gist_en: When an administrative agency may make a decision adverse to another person in an administrative reconsideration, if it fails to notify that person to participate in the administrative reconsideration in an appropriate manner before making the reconsideration decision, it constitutes a serious violation of legal procedures and shall be revoked.
keywords_en: Administrative; Administrative Reconsideration; First Instance; Intermediate People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Natural Person; Administrative Reconsideration Law; Interim Measures for Registration of Ownership of Urban Houses; Violation of Administrative Reconsideration Procedure; Obligation to Notify for Participation in Reconsideration; Reconsideration Period; Revocation of Reconsideration Decision; House Registration; Inheritance Dispute; Due Process; Land Use Rights; Administrative Litigation
full_text_en:
Zhang Chengyin v. Xuzhou Municipal People's Government — dispute over administrative reconsideration decision on house registration

Ruling Summary

Where an administrative organ may make a decision adverse to another person during administrative reconsideration, if it renders the reconsideration decision without notifying that person to participate in the reconsideration in an appropriate manner, this constitutes a serious violation of legal procedures and the decision shall be revoked.

Plaintiff: Zhang Chengyin, female, 69 years old, residing in Dongyuan Residential Quarter, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Xuzhou Municipal People's Government, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Li Fuquan, Mayor of the City.

Third Party: Cao Chunfang, female, 70 years old, retired employee, residing in Fushui Residential Quarter, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, sister-in-law of the plaintiff's husband.

Third Party: Cao Chunyi, male, 73 years old, retired employee, residing in Dongyuan Residential Quarter, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, husband of the plaintiff.

The defendant, Xuzhou Municipal People's Government, accepted the application for administrative reconsideration filed by the third party Cao Chunfang on October 28, 2003, and made the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 on April 29, 2004, on the grounds that upon the death of Cao Chenshi, the user of the house at No. 31 Min'an Lane, Xuzhou City, in 1986, Zhang Chengyin was not the lawful heir to the property; the former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Real Estate Bureau) had found that Zhang Chengyin had obtained the property right of the house at No. 31 Min'an Lane by original acquisition, which was inconsistent with the facts; the issuance of the House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 to Zhang Chengyin violated Article 8 of the Interim Measures for the Registration of Urban House Ownership; and the confirmation of the house property right and state-owned land use right of No. 31 Min'an Lane to Zhang Chengyin was improper. Accordingly, pursuant to Items 1 and 5 of Subparagraph (3) of Paragraph 1 of Article 28 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, the decision confirmed that the specific administrative act of the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau in confirming the house property right and state-owned land use right of No. 31 Min'an Lane to Zhang Chengyin was illegal. Zhang Chengyin, dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff alleged: The former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau issued the House Ownership Certificate to her in 1988, and Cao Chunfang applied for administrative reconsideration in 2004, which exceeded the statutory time limit for applying for administrative reconsideration; the reconsideration organ had no basis for accepting the application; as the administrative reconsideration organ, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government, in determining that upon the death of Cao Chenshi, Cao Chunfang and Cao Chunyi had the right to inherit the disputed property according to law and that she was not the lawful heir to the property, exceeded its authority; the reconsideration decision failed to ascertain the amount of property left by Cao Chenshi at the time of her death, making the facts unclear. She requested the revocation of the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government.

Evidence provided by the plaintiff:

1. The Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government on April 29, 2004, to prove the existence of the specific administrative act sued.
2. Testimonies of witnesses Zhu Derong and Li Ruitang, to prove that the disputed house was self-built by Zhang Chengyin and constituted original acquisition.
3. Archival materials of the House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 issued to Zhang Chengyin by the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration on September 28, 1988, to prove the legality of the issuance.
4. Archival materials of the House Ownership Certificate No. 104027 issued to Zhang Chengyin by the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration on September 5, 1991; archival materials of the House Ownership Certificate No. 112014 issued on June 1, 1994; archival materials of the House Ownership Certificate No. Shifangzi 97300783 issued on February 19, 1997; and the House Ownership Certificate No. 98301991 issued on December 8, 1998, to prove the evolution of the property and ownership registration at No. 31 Min'an Lane, that the defendant's review target was erroneous, and that Cao Chunfang should have long known that the property right of No. 31 Min'an Lane had been registered in Zhang Chengyin's name, making the application for reconsideration beyond the statutory time limit.

The defendant argued: The municipal government had repeatedly telephoned Zhang Chengyin to participate in the reconsideration, but she refused, so it should be deemed that she had waived her rights; Cao Chunfang had not known until recently that Zhang Chengyin had obtained the House Ownership Certificate for No. 31 Min'an Lane in 1988, so the application for reconsideration was not time-barred; upon the death of Cao Chenshi, the user of the house at No. 31 Min'an Lane, in 1986, Cao Chunfang and Cao Chunyi had the right to inherit the property according to law, and Zhang Chengyin was not the lawful heir and should not have become the owner of the property; the former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau had erroneously determined that Zhang Chengyin had obtained the property right by original acquisition and registered the property in her name, violating Article 8 of the Interim Measures for the Registration of Urban House Ownership, which constituted improper confirmation; the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 had clear findings of fact and correct application of law.

Evidence submitted by the defendant:

1. The application for administrative reconsideration and supplementary explanation written by Cao Chunfang on October 28, 2003, the reply of the Xuzhou Real Estate Bureau to the administrative reconsideration, and the notice dated February 26, 2004, to Zhang Chengyin to participate in the administrative reconsideration, to prove the legality of the procedure for making the sued reconsideration decision.
2. The archival materials of the House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 issued to Zhang Chengyin by the Xuzhou Real Estate Bureau on September 28, 1988, and the household registration certificate for No. 31 Min'an Lane and the death certificate for Cao Chenshi obtained by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government from the Heping Police Station of the Xuzhou Public Security Bureau, to prove that the former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau's determination in 1988 that Zhang Chengyin had obtained the property right of No. 31 Min'an Lane by original acquisition, and the issuance of House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741, were inadequately supported by evidence.

Evidence submitted by the third party Cao Chunfang:

Testimonies of witnesses Zhu Zhenxiang, Qiu Yulan, Si Xuelan, and Ji Changlan, to prove that the house registered under House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 issued to Zhang Chengyin by the former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau in 1988 was part of Cao Chenshi's estate.

The third party Cao Chunyi did not submit any evidence.

The Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

Cao Chunyi and Cao Chunfang are siblings. Their father died early, and they lived with their mother, Cao Chenshi, at No. 31 Min'an Lane, Xuzhou City, which originally consisted of three east thatched rooms and one south thatched room. In 1954, Zhang Chengyin married Cao Chunyi and moved into No. 31 Min'an Lane. Around 1961, Cao Chunfang married and moved out of No. 31 Min'an Lane. On January 30, 1986, Cao Chenshi died. During the period when Cao Chenshi lived together with her daughter-in-law Zhang Chengyin and her family members, the original residence at No. 31 Min'an Lane was renovated and newly built, resulting in a total of seven rooms of brick-wood and brick-concrete structures. Among them, the three east rooms of brick-concrete structure were rebuilt on the basis of the original three east thatched rooms in December 1981 under Construction Permit No. 2268 issued in the name of Zhang Chengyin. On May 31, 1988, Zhang Chengyin submitted a written application to the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration to register the property rights and land use rights for the above seven rooms at No. 31 Min'an Lane. The Gulou District Real Estate Registration and Certification Office of Xuzhou, after investigating the application materials submitted by Zhang Chengyin, issued House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 to Zhang Chengyin on September 28, 1988, affixed with the seal of the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government, and registered 199.78 square meters of state-owned land use right for Zhang Chengyin.

Thereafter, the house at No. 31 Min'an Lane underwent new construction in 1991, expansion in 1994, a gift in 1997, and new construction in 1998. The Xuzhou Real Estate Administration, after public notice and finding no objections to the property rights, correspondingly carried out property right registration for Zhang Chengyin and issued house ownership certificates. The Xuzhou Land Administration Bureau also issued a state-owned land use certificate to Zhang Chengyin on December 3, 1996. In 2002, the house of Zhang Chengyin at No. 31 Min'an Lane was lawfully demolished. On October 28, 2003, Cao Chunfang applied to the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government for administrative reconsideration, requesting the revocation of the specific administrative act that confirmed and registered the house property right and land use right of No. 31 Min'an Lane to Zhang Chengyin in 1988. The Xuzhou Municipal People's Government made the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 on April 29, 2004, confirming that the specific administrative act of the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau (the predecessor of the respondent Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau) in confirming the house property right and state-owned land use right of No. 31 Min'an Lane to Zhang Chengyin was illegal.

The Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province held: In September 1988, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government issued House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 to the plaintiff Zhang Chengyin in accordance with the Interim Measures for the Registration of Urban House Ownership promulgated by the former Ministry of Urban and Rural Construction and Environmental Protection on April 21, 1987. According to subsequent administrative regulations and legal provisions, the authority to issue house ownership certificates in Xuzhou was exercised by the current Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau. The legal consequences of the administrative act of the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government in issuing House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 to Zhang Chengyin should be borne by the current Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau. Therefore, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government had jurisdiction over Cao Chunfang's reconsideration application.

In this case, after Cao Chenshi, mother of Cao Chunfang, died on January 30, 1986, the property at No. 31 Min'an Lane, Xuzhou City, had been occupied and used by Zhang Chengyin and her family; Zhang Chengyin and her family had built new houses and expanded existing houses there in the 1990s. Before the former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau issued a house ownership certificate for this property to Zhang Chengyin in 1994, it also conducted a public notice to solicit any objections from interested parties regarding the property rights. Cao Chunfang should have known that the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration had confirmed and registered the property right of No. 31 Min'an Lane to Zhang Chengyin. Therefore, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government's acceptance of Cao Chunfang's reconsideration application filed on October 28, 2003, and making the reconsideration decision exceeded the statutory time limit; Cao Chunfang's claim that she only learned in October 2003 that the former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration had confirmed and registered the property right of No. 31 Min'an Lane to Zhang Chengyin was not supported by law. Although an administrative organ may adopt a written review method when conducting administrative reconsideration, Zhang Chengyin, as the holder of House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 issued by the former Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau in 1988, had a direct interest in the outcome of the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government's review of that certificate. The Xuzhou Municipal People's Government should have notified Zhang Chengyin to participate in the administrative reconsideration. Since the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government could not prove that it had taken appropriate measures to notify Zhang Chengyin to participate in the administrative reconsideration, this constituted a serious violation of administrative procedures. Moreover, the conclusion of the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 also had a defect in that the target of the reconsideration review was not specific.

In summary, the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government upon accepting Cao Chunfang's reconsideration application seriously violated legal procedures and should be revoked according to law. Pursuant to Article 9, Paragraph 1, and Article 10, Paragraph 3 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, and Item 3 of Subparagraph (2) of Article 54 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the Xuzhou People's Court rendered judgment on September 30, 2004:

Revoke the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government on April 29, 2004.

After the judgment was pronounced, Cao Chunfang, dissatisfied, appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court.

Main grounds of appeal by Cao Chunfang: The trial court's finding that she should have known in 1994 that the house at No. 31 Min'an Lane had been confirmed to Zhang Chengyin was inconsistent with the facts, and its determination that her application for administrative reconsideration on October 28, 2003, exceeded the statutory time limit was erroneous. The trial court's finding that the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government violated legal procedures in the reconsideration was incorrect. During the reconsideration, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government repeatedly notified Zhang Chengyin to participate, but she refused. Therefore, the reconsideration decision made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government under circumstances where Zhang Chengyin intentionally did not participate did not constitute a violation of legal procedures. Requested the revocation of the trial judgment and affirmation of the reconsideration decision of the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government.

Zhang Chengyin argued: Cao Chunfang knew as early as 1994 that the house at No. 31 Min'an Lane was registered in Zhang Chengyin's name; the trial court's finding that her application for administrative reconsideration exceeded the statutory time limit was correct. The Xuzhou Municipal People's Government failed to notify her to participate in the reconsideration by statutory means, which violated legal procedures. The current houses at No. 31 Min'an Lane, Xuzhou City, were all built by her and had nothing to do with the appellant Cao Chunfang. Requested the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the trial judgment.

Cao Chunyi did not submit a written defense, but expressed agreement with Zhang Chengyin's defense during the trial.

The Xuzhou Municipal People's Government stated: The provisions of the Administrative Reconsideration Law regarding third parties are flexible clauses; whether a third party participates in administrative reconsideration is decided by the reconsideration organ based on the circumstances. In this case, Zhang Chengyin did not participate in the reconsideration, which cannot be used to conclude that the reconsideration organ violated legal procedures. The Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government did not violate the procedures stipulated in the Administrative Reconsideration Law. The acceptance of the administrative reconsideration in this case did not exceed the statutory time limit. Requested the revocation of the trial judgment and affirmation of the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government.

The Jiangsu High People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

The trial court, based on the stubs of the public notice for soliciting objections to property rights, determined that the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau had conducted a property rights public notice before issuing the house ownership certificate to Zhang Chengyin, and thereby presumed that the appellant Cao Chunfang should have known in 1994 that the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration had confirmed the house at No. 31 Min'an Lane to Zhang Chengyin. This reasoning was insufficient and therefore not confirmed. Facts not disputed by all parties were confirmed according to law.

The main focus of dispute in this case was: When an administrative organ reviews an administrative decision under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, if it may directly affect the interests of another person, must it notify that person to participate in the reconsideration and hear their opinions in an appropriate manner?

The Jiangsu High People's Court held:

I. Although House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741 involved in this case was issued by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government in September 1988, according to subsequent relevant laws and regulations, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government no longer had the authority to issue house ownership certificates. At the time Cao Chunfang applied for reconsideration, the authority to issue house ownership certificates in Xuzhou was exercised by the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau. Therefore, the legal consequences of the act of issuing the house ownership certificate by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government should be borne by the current certificate-issuing authority, the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau. Cao Chunfang, dissatisfied with the issuance of House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741, filed an application for reconsideration, and the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau should be the respondent. The trial court's finding that the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government had jurisdiction over Cao Chunfang's reconsideration application was correct.

II. Although the Administrative Reconsideration Law does not explicitly require the reconsideration organ to notify a third party to participate in the reconsideration, according to the requirements of due process, when an administrative organ may make an administrative decision adverse to another person, it should specifically hear the opinions of the interested party. In this case, the subject of the reconsideration organ's review was the act of issuing House Ownership Certificate No. Gufangzi 1741, and the outcome of the reconsideration decision had a direct interest in the current certificate holder, Zhang Chengyin. Therefore, the reconsideration organ should have formally notified Zhang Chengyin to participate in the reconsideration. In this case, although the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government claimed that it had orally notified Zhang Chengyin to participate in the administrative reconsideration by telephone, it could not prove this, and the interested party disputed it. It should be found that the government did not take appropriate measures to formally notify the party to participate in the administrative reconsideration. Therefore, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government's reason for finding that Zhang Chengyin voluntarily waived her right to participate in the reconsideration was not well-founded. Under these circumstances, the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government made an administrative reconsideration decision adverse to the interested party without hearing her opinions, which constituted a serious violation of legal procedures.

III. According to the relevant provisions of the Administrative Reconsideration Law and the Civil Procedure Law, when exercising the power of administrative reconsideration, the reconsideration organ should review the legality and appropriateness of the specific administrative act that is the subject of the reconsideration application. Disputes over civil rights and interests should be resolved through civil litigation procedures. In this case, the reconsideration decision made by the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government directly confirmed the civil rights disputed by the relevant parties, which exceeded the authority of the reconsideration organ and lacked legal basis, and should be revoked.

In summary, the trial judgment revoking the Administrative Reconsideration Decision No. Xuzhengxingjue [2004] 24 of the Xuzhou Municipal People's Government was correct and should be affirmed. The grounds of appeal of the appellant Cao Chunfang were untenable.

Pursuant to Item (1) of Article 61 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered judgment on December 10, 2004:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.
